subject: Zenith Health trial - hosting options, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T16:18:00Z
Subject: Zenith Health trial - hosting options, success criteria & next steps

Hi Alicia / Ken —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed playbook so we can lock the trial plan: the goal is to validate latency and PHI-safe routing for your triage assistant and to measure throughput for peak-hour batch scoring.

Key hosting options we outlined:
- Hosted API (fastest): Redwood-managed hosted endpoints. Good for quick functional validation with synthetic or de-identified data.
- Dedicated sandbox: Reserved GPU pool in our tenant for higher throughput and predictable latency; good intermediate step if you want isolation without full VPC.
- VPC/private trial: Customer-managed VPC peering or private deployment for PHI workflows; required if you need inbound-only access and your security team insists on no egress of raw data.

Suggested success criteria (please flag additions):
1) Latency: p95 token latency <= 350ms at 2 concurrent sessions for routing prompts.
2) Throughput: sustained 20 qps for batch scoring jobs (50 token avg).
3) Correctness: end-to-end classification precision >= 90% on agreed eval set.
4) Security: SOC2 evidence + VPC connection test for PHI step.

Proposed timeline and owners (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize hosting choice & sign off on SOW (Owners: Alicia/Zenith procurement, Naomi).
- Week 1: Hosted sanity run with synthetic data (Owners: Naomi, Marissa).
- Week 2-3: Dedicated sandbox spin-up (if chosen) or VPC setup/peering (if VPC chosen) (Owners: Rishi, Zenith infra).
- Week 4: Evaluation window and final report (Owners: Naomi, Marissa, Zenith PM).

Immediate asks for you (Alicia / Ken):
- Confirm whether Zenith requires PHI on day 1 (affects hosting choice).
- Provide a contact for networking (VPN/VPC) and procurement PO timeline.

I attached a short POC scope and a network requirements worksheet. If you prefer a two-step approach, we can run hosted first to validate behavior (synthetic), then flip to VPC for PHI testing.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync early next week to confirm the hosting path and owners? I propose Mon 06/14 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the clear recap. Short answers:
- Yes, we will be testing with PHI in the evaluation phase. Our security team will not approve any egress of raw PHI outside our VPC.
- We have an infra contact: Ken Lo (cc'd). Procurement is targetting a PO within 3 weeks but we may need a short SOW to attach — can you provide a template?

Success criteria look good, but add a security acceptance check: complete Redwood security questionnaire + penetration test scheduling window.

We prefer to avoid lengthy sandbox migrations. Our strong preference is: run an initial hosted functional smoke with synthetic data (to validate prompts & model behavior) and then switch to a VPC-private trial for PHI. That will minimize time to first feedback but meet our compliance needs.

Mon 06/14 10:00am PT works for a short sync.

Thanks,
Alicia

alicia@zenithhealth.com

Thanks Alicia — that flow makes sense and is the path I recommended in the call. A few clarifications and next actions:

Plan (updated):
- Day 0-3: Hosted smoke with synthetic data to validate prompt templates, token costs, and initial latency numbers. No PHI involved. (Owner: Naomi, Marissa)
- Day 4-14: VPC/private trial setup: VPC peering and private endpoint, security questionnaire response, and connectivity testing (Owners: Rishi, Ken).
- Day 15-28: PHI evaluation window in private trial; run agreed eval set and throughput tests (Owners: Zenith PM, Naomi).

Deliverables we will provide:
- SOW template for your procurement (attached)
- Security questionnaire + SOC2 package (will upload link to Drive prior to the Monday sync)
- Test harness and sample eval set definition for the precision/recall run

Open items for Monday sync:
1) Ken: confirm VPC peering windows (dates/times when your infra can accept peering config).
2) Procurement: confirm PO timing and any redline needs to SOW.
3) Security: confirm if you require penetration testing scope or just a scheduled test after connectivity.

If we get procurement + Ken's peering slot this week we can aim to start the VPC setup on Wed (06/16). Linking the POC ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-4827.

See you Monday — I'll send the calendar invite for 06/14 10:00am PT with a short agenda.

Best,
Naomi

Looping in technical notes and a conservative ops plan. I built a short checklist and cost estimate (attached). Key points:

Network & connectivity (for VPC trial):
- Required: 1 outbound TLS 443 for control plane only, VPC peering for data path (no internet egress for PHI).
- CIDR ranges we need from Zenith: 2 x /24 (for subnets + NAT).
- Test window: allow 2 hours for routing table & peering validation; schedule during low traffic.

Dedicated vs VPC cost delta (high level):
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPUs): predictable hourly cost; estimated burn $4.2k/week for baseline configuration (included in attached dedicated_capacity_estimate.csv).
- VPC/private: marginally higher setup effort (network engineering) but same runtime costs once established.

Action items for Redwood ops:
- I will provision a dedicated sandbox template for this config so we can fallback quickly if VPC setup gets delayed.
- Prep security questionnaire answers and SOC2 bundle (Marissa, can you confirm current bundle version?).

Attachments referenced: network_requirements.xlsx, dedicated_capacity_estimate.csv

I'll join the Monday call if scheduled.

-rishi
